title: Bar Graph Interpretation
tagline: Year 2 — Multi-series bar charts: reading, comparing, percentage change and ratios

introduction.overview: A bar graph shows values as bars whose heights are proportional to the quantities. In Year 2 you meet multi-series bar graphs, where several bars sit side by side for each year or category. Questions combine reading values with totals, differences, averages, percentage changes and ratios. The data is the same as in a table; the picture only makes comparison easier.
introduction.placementRelevance: Bar graph sets are commonly asked in company aptitude rounds. In an exam you read the heights from the picture; here the values are given as a table so that you can practise the calculations.
introduction.realWorldContext: Production reports, sales comparisons and annual dashboards use multi-series bar charts.

learningObjectives: Read exact values from multi-series bars using the scale
Compute totals, differences and averages across series and years
Compute percentage change and share of total
Compare growth across series and years
Use approximation when options are far apart

prerequisiteKnowledge.quickRefresher: Percentage change = (new − old) ÷ old × 100. Share = part ÷ total × 100. Ratio a : b is simplified by dividing both terms by their HCF.

coreDefinitions: Series: one set of bars of the same colour (one company or category).
Scale: the value of one unit of the axis.
Year-on-year (YoY) change: change from one year to the next.
Share of total: a value as a percentage of the sum of all series in that year.
Base: the quantity a percentage is measured against.
conceptExplanation.theoreticalIntuition: A multi-series bar chart is a table drawn with bars. Write the numbers into a small table, then every question is arithmetic on a few cells. The most common errors are reading a wrong bar and using the wrong base for a percentage.
conceptExplanation.visualOrMentalModel: Write down the values for each series and year. Underline what the question asks (which series, which year, total or difference) and use only those cells.

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Total and difference
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: Total = sum of series in a year;  Difference = one series − another

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Average
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: Average = Sum ÷ number of years (or series)

mainNarrative: First convert the graph to numbers. With three series (A, B, C) and five years, write a 5 × 3 table of the values. After that every question refers to specific cells.
For totals and differences, choose the year. The total production in 2023 is 66 + 58 + 45 = 169 thousand. The difference between A and C in 2022 is 60 − 38 = 22 thousand.
For averages, divide by the number of terms: the average of A over five years is (40 + 48 + 45 + 60 + 66) ÷ 5 = 51.8 thousand.
For percentage change, use the earlier value as the base: A rose from 40 to 66, an increase of 26 ÷ 40 = 65%. For a share, divide by that year's total: B in 2022 is 52 ÷ 150 = 34.7% of the total.
To find the year with the largest change, compute the year-on-year changes of the series. A changed by +8, −3, +15 and +6, so the greatest rise was in 2022.

deepDiveAspects.title: Reading from the picture
deepDiveAspects.content: In an exam the heights fall on gridlines or midway between them. Read to the nearest half-division and note the scale before reading values.

deepDiveAspects.title: Percentage points vs percentages
deepDiveAspects.content: If a share rises from 30% to 35%, it rises by 5 percentage points but by about 16.7% in percentage terms. Read the question to see which is asked.

solvedExamples.title: Total of a year
solvedExamples.question: Using the bar data, find the total production of the three companies in 2023.

solvedExamples.title: Percentage change
solvedExamples.question: By what percentage did company A's production increase from 2019 to 2023?

solvedExamples.title: Share of total
solvedExamples.question: What percentage of the total production in 2022 was produced by B (to one decimal place)?
solvedExamples.whyItWorks: The total for that year is the base.
solvedExamples.commonTrap: Using the total of all years.

shortcutMethods.title: Table first, then choose cells

traditionalVsShortcut.traditionalMethod: Read the graph for every question.
traditionalVsShortcut.shortcutMethod: Convert the graph to a small table, underline what is asked and pick only those cells. Use approximation when options are spread.

rulesForApplication: Percentage change: old is the base.

placementTips.eliminationTechnique: Use rough values to reject options far from the estimate.
placementTips.questionSelectionAdvice: Do direct and total questions first.
placementTips.recruiterInsight: The same table can be reused for all questions in the set.
